extensions.provenance: Recorded after the build (palette "Violet night") from style.css, landing.css, landing.js, index.html, welcome.html, account.html, emergency.html, trips.html, signin.html, app.js and tests/landing.spec.js. Rendered evidence: .impeccable/review/*.png, Playwright captures of the real app against a throwaway local server with simulated GPS. landing-desktop-hero.png, landing-mobile-full.png and tracker-desktop.png were copied from the session scratchpad design/l1 captures taken after the Violet night palette and /welcome shipped; the other review images predate the palette change.

motion.name: landing-loops
motion.value: check-in deplete 7s, SOS ping 2.6s, queue rise 3.2s

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Stops every animation on every page; landing SVGs paused at their finished frame; tests/landing.spec.js asserts zero running animations.

conditionTones.idle: Grey dot, Raised Charcoal band, Hairline edge: not recording.
conditionTones.calm: Working Violet: recording and reaching the server; the dot breathes.
conditionTones.attention: Attention Amber: offline, stale GPS, paused or delayed trip, uploads waiting, storage failing, permission denied while recording.
conditionTones.alert: Alarm Red: SOS countdown, sending, queued or active; check-in requested. Alert outranks attention, attention outranks calm.

extensions.motionBudget: The tracker stays nearly still (battery); motion lives on the landing and sign-in pages.

sections: Aurora: three drifting blurred colour fields
Hero with animated device preview of the real tracker (band cycles calm, attention offline, calm back online; SVG route draw; SMIL pin)
How it works: three numbered steps with a filling rail
Feature bands: Trip check-in timer, SOS waves and countdown with honest delivery states, offline queue rising
What Safe Location will never do: ruled two-column list
Closing CTA with Call 112, hairline footer
landing.reveals: Content visible by default; hidden-then-revealed only when landing.js adds .motion.

narrative.overview:
Safe Location reads like an instrument panel on a dark violet night, not a dashboard of equal cards. One live panel answers "am I being recorded, and is it reaching anyone?" before anything else: a single condition band carries the overall tone in one plain sentence, a large state line names what is happening, and a ruled grid of label-over-value readouts gives the evidence. Everything else (map, trip, recording settings, backup, details, history) sits below or beside it at lower weight.

Density is moderate and calm. Panels are charcoal-violet sheets divided by hairline rules rather than stacks of floating cards; colour is almost entirely neutral until something needs a person's attention, and then it appears in exactly one place, with one meaning. The face is Geist, self-hosted and small (29 KB for Latin), so the product reads like a modern SaaS tool without a font service; text shows at once in the system font and swaps when Geist arrives. Behind everything lies the signal field: soft violet light falling from the top of the screen with a faint pink glow at one corner, a point grid like a map graticule, and fine grain.

Motion follows a budget. The tracker stays open for hours on a phone battery, so it is nearly still: colour changes ease over 400ms and the only thing that moves on its own is the breathing dot while recording is healthy. Motion lives on the short-visit pages: the sign-in veil breathes, and the public landing page at /welcome (a Persuade-mode page in the same world) drifts an aurora and animates a preview of the real tracker.

The world is honest about uncertainty. Readings show their age and accuracy in tabular numerals, gaps are drawn as dashed lines, doubtful points are amber and left off the route, and nothing in the copy claims a message was delivered unless the provider confirmed it. The landing page's previews only show states the product really shows.
keyCharacteristics: One tone-carrying condition band per screen, driven by state (idle grey, calm violet, attention amber, alert red).
Hairline-ruled grids and sheets with ruled sections instead of card stacks.
Violet means working, amber means attention, red means emergency, failure or irreversible removal.
Geist (self-hosted, system fallback), weights 600 to 750, tabular numerals for every reading.
The signal field background: violet light from above, a pink side glow, a fading point grid, grain. CSS only.
Flat, bordered surfaces in the tracker; depth only on map controls and markers.
A tall red SOS always within thumb reach, with "Call 112" under it.
Motion budget: the tracker nearly still, motion on the landing and sign-in pages, all of it off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Red Means Danger Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for an emergency (SOS, Call 112, alert tone, check-in requested), a failure (denied permission, rejected upload, error) or an irreversible removal (delete, remove, clear, cancel trip). Removal is outline-only red unless it is the confirmed final submit. A merely doubtful reading is amber, never red.

rules.name: The One Meaning Per Hue Rule
rules.body: Violet is working state, amber is attention, green is confirmed fact. A hue never borrows another's meaning, and state is never carried by colour alone: every tone has a sentence or a label. Aurora Pink is light, not a state, so it carries no meaning at all.

rules.name: The Tabular Reading Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates (times, countdowns, accuracy, coordinates, counts) is set with tabular numerals so live readings tick without layout shift. This holds inside the landing previews too.

rules.name: The Light Font Rule
rules.body: One self-hosted family only (Geist), subset by script and loaded with `swap`, so text never waits for a download. No font services, no icon fonts, no second display family.

rules.name: The Instrument First Rule
rules.body: On every viewport the condition band, state line and readouts come before the map, with SOS beside them within thumb reach.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Stacked Rule
rules.body: Group related panels as one sheet whose sections are divided by hairlines, and lay readings on a grid whose 1px gaps show the border colour. Do not stack floating, shadowed cards.

rules.name: The Motion Budget Rule
rules.body: The tracker stays nearly still because it runs for hours on a phone battery: only the calm-tone breathing dot, the map spinner and short colour transitions. Ambient motion belongs to short-visit pages (sign-in, landing). Everywhere, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` stops every animation, and content never depends on motion to be visible.

dos: **Do** let one condition band per screen carry the overall tone, with a plain sentence that names what is happening.
**Do** use Working Violet for working state, Attention Amber for attention, and red only for emergency, failure and irreversible removal.
**Do** keep Aurora Pink as light only: field glows, aurora, rail ends; never a fill, text colour or state.
**Do** set every live reading in tabular numerals at 650 weight, label over value, on a hairline-ruled grid.
**Do** group related sections into one sheet divided by 1px hairlines.
**Do** keep primary controls at least 44px tall and keep accessible names when a label is visually hidden.
**Do** honour reduced motion everywhere: stop the breathing dot, spinner, veil, aurora, previews and colour transitions, and keep content visible without motion or JavaScript.
**Do** make landing previews show only states the product really shows, in the same honest delivery language.
**Do** show age and accuracy with every location and say "simulated" or "submitted" until a provider confirms delivery.
donts: **Don't** use red for a doubtful reading such as a GPS jump or low accuracy; that is amber.
**Don't** add ambient motion to the tracker; the breathing dot in the calm tone is the only thing that moves there on its own. Motion belongs to the landing and sign-in pages.
**Don't** add eyebrows or kickers (small uppercase labels above headings); section titles stand alone in sentence case.
**Don't** stack shadowed, same-weight cards where a ruled sheet will do, and don't carry landing glows and shadows into the tracker.
**Don't** add font services, a second family or icon fonts; use self-hosted Geist and inline SVG icons.
**Don't** claim a message was delivered, or that someone is safe or in danger, without provider confirmation or the person's own action.
**Don't** fabricate streets, routes, accuracy or results to fill an empty state; say what is unknown.
